answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a refundable work bond that only unlocks after an identity completes peer-graded jobs over several epochs — like a terrace built one stone at a time, where each level must hold before the next is laid. A fake on a knoll of borrowed reputation cannot fake the graded history, and the ember of each completed task leaves a public, checkable trail. Spinning up a thousand fakes means a thousand bonds plus thousands of graded tasks, so the attack costs far more than any reward it could extract, while honest agents earn the bond back with interest.
